title: Daytona Cost Existence Check via Linear Scan
approach_explanation: The problem asks whether a specific element 'k' appears at least once in a given array of size 'n'. Since the subsegment property of the problem implies that if 'k' exists anywhere in the array, we can always choose a subsegment containing 'k' (even the whole array or just a singleton containing 'k') as the most frequent element, the problem simplifies to checking if 'k' is present in the input array. We can perform a simple linear scan over the elements and set a boolean flag if 'k' is encountered.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases 't' and loops 't' times to process each test case independently.
Reads the array size 'n' and the target integer 'k'. Initializes a boolean flag 'exists' to false.
Iterates through the 'n' elements of the array. If any element matches 'k', sets 'exists' to true.
Outputs "YES" if 'exists' is true, and "NO" otherwise, followed by a newline.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each testcase, we iterate through the array of size $N$ exactly once. If there are $T$ test cases and the sum of $N$ is bounded by standard competitive programming limits, the total time complexity is $O(\sum N)$, which runs well within standard time limits.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: We do not store the array elements in memory; instead, we process each element on the fly using a single integer variable. Thus, extra auxiliary space is $O(1)$.

strengths: Extremely memory efficient by avoiding array storage.
Clear and straightforward logic mapping directly to the problem constraints.
Fast I/O implicitly used via standard streams.
edge_cases_handled: Single-element arrays containing or not containing 'k'.

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Instead of reading all remaining elements once 'k' is found, we can break early or consume the rest of the line. However, since all inputs must be read to move to the next testcase, a full loop or reading remainder is still required.
